title: Velocity Checkpoint
premise: A neon-styled microgame where the player helps a speedster clear a checkpoint by calculating the missing final velocity from a simple motion formula.
interaction_model: Single-screen numeric input quiz with button or Enter-key submission, instant validation, unlimited retries, and audiovisual success/failure feedback.
objective: Compute the correct final speed from the provided starting speed, acceleration, and time values, then submit the exact answer to clear the checkpoint.
progression: Static one-question loop with no additional stages, score system, or unlock tree; progression is limited to retrying until the single checkpoint is solved.
theme: Futuristic neon runner framed as an arcade race checkpoint.
mood: Energetic, lightweight, encouraging, and arcade-like with mild educational focus.
likely_audience: Casual players who enjoy tiny quiz-like web games
Mobile-first users who benefit from quick tap interactions
confidence_notes: High confidence that the implemented mechanic is a single fixed educational calculation challenge.
High confidence that the racing/runner framing is thematic presentation rather than a true movement-based runner mechanic.
Moderate confidence that the project may have been intended as part of a broader lesson or checkpoint series, but only one prompt is implemented here.
recreation_prompt: Create a single-screen browser microgame called "Velocity Checkpoint" that wraps a basic physics formula quiz in a neon arcade runner presentation. The player should see a futuristic race briefing, a one-row motion table with starting speed, acceleration, and time already filled in, and one empty numeric field for the final speed using the formula v = u + a × t. Use values equivalent to 5 m/s, 2 m/s², and 4 s so the correct answer is 13 m/s. The gameplay loop should be very short: read the table, enter a number, press a large Check Answer button or hit Enter, then receive immediate feedback and retry if wrong. Treat the race theme as cosmetic framing rather than actual running mechanics. Include a status area, clear success and failure result text, celebratory versus corrective reaction copy, and a compact docked animated reaction panel that never blocks the input. Add an arcade-style ambient background loop that only starts after the player interacts, plus separate click, blocked, success, fail, and level-clear sound effects. On correct answers, show a checkpoint-cleared style message and layered positive audio; on wrong or empty submissions, show error feedback and a fail-style reaction. Present everything inside a polished responsive sci-fi card with glowing cyan/blue accents, readable typography, and mobile-safe controls that stack cleanly on small screens.
